findings.finding: Revolve filed an 8-K (Item 8.01, filed 2026-10-30) disclosing unauthorized access in which an actor obtained, 'through automated means', the names, contact information, card numbers and expiration dates of customers with saved payment details. Texas breach filings alone list 127,200 affected residents (The Record, 2026-10-30). The company says it expects no material impact, and the call is the first chance for analysts to ask about costs, reserves, card-network fines, litigation and any Q4 conversion hit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior cyber incident at this company. The stock fell -2.86% on 2026-10-30 (934k shares against a ~695k 20d average) and -1.92% on 2026-11-02 (stockanalysis price history), about -4.7% over two sessions after the disclosure.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the ~4.7% two-day fall is the market's first read. Not yet disclosed are the total count (Texas 127,200 implies a national figure in the high hundreds of thousands to low millions against 3.04M active customers, which is an inference), any Q4 charge, and whether saved-card removal hurts repeat conversion. If the market had fully priced a costly outcome, the implied move and put demand would sit far above the name's history. The put OI is extreme (P/C 37.8), but the implied move of 12.0% is within the 13.9% max reaction.
findings.independence: The Record, 2026-10-30, https://therecord.media/resolve-fashion-retailer-data-breach-payment-cards, reports the same incident with state counts (Texas 127,200, Vermont 1,328). It rests on the same company disclosure. No law-firm investigation was found.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue should land near the bar. July net sales were +18% y/y (company), and consensus $344.8M implies +16.6% against an easy Q3 2025 comp (+4.4%). The last two quarters' first-month figures were +16% (first 7 weeks of Q1, Q1 landed +16%) and +14% (April, Q2 landed +12%), so a ~2-point fade from July lands at about $343M, inside the bar. On a two-year stack, Q3 consensus (~21%) equals Q2's (~21-22%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue $347.4M beat (+12%), and the stock fell -4.06%. Q1 2026: +16% revenue, April +14%, and the stock fell -13.87%. Q3 2025: revenue missed (+4.4%) on a margin beat, and the stock rose +11.01%. Revenue has not decided this stock's direction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: consensus already embeds the July +18% with a shade of fade. The only unpriced part is how much Aug-Sep slowed or held, which no free traffic or card series covers for 2026.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001746618/000119312526206442/rvlv-ex99_1.htm, April +14% leading to Q2 +12%) gives the fade pattern. That is a different document but the same company.

findings.finding: The Q3 gross-margin guide of 53.5-54.0% (-88bp y/y at the midpoint, explained by a tough comp) looks conservative. Underlying Q2 GM excluding refunds was ~55.0% against a 54.1-54.6% guide, about 40-90bp above the top. Separately, the CFO said $1.4M of further IEEPA refund claims were 'not received or included in our financials or guidance', worth roughly 40bp of Q3 GM if received in the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: a margin-led beat on a sales miss bought +11.01%. Q2 2026: a 56.6% GM against a 54.1-54.6% guide (refund-aided) still fell -4.06%. Margin beats have paid once and been sold once.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the sell side knows the company beats its GM guide. The $1.4M refund is a one-off and too small to matter much (~$0.015 EPS). If the market expected a clear GM beat, EPS consensus would sit above the guide-implied ~$0.21. The two EPS sources disagree ($0.21 against $0.23), so this is capped small.
findings.independence: Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001746618/000119312526332838/rvlv-ex99_1.htm) carries the 162bp refund benefit and the 54.1-54.6% prior guide. This is the same company's documents and the same event.

findings.finding: Opex has run over guidance two quarters running, and the forward guide is the line this stock sells on. Q2 marketing was 16.5% of sales against a 15.7% guide, S&D was 17.9% ('slightly above our guidance range') and G&A was 'slightly above plan'. FY marketing was raised to 15.8-16.0% and G&A to $170-172M. Q4 marketing is pre-flagged 'north of 16%', and growth initiatives cost ~2 points of adjusted EBITDA margin in 2026. A Q3 overshoot of the 15.0% marketing guide, or a 2027 investment signal, is the likeliest negative on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (marketing 15.8% against 14.3% the prior year, Los Angeles label investment): -13.87% on an EPS beat. Q2 2026 (marketing raised, G&A raised): -4.06% on an EPS beat of $0.26 against $0.20. The baseline shows 1 up of 7 reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q4 marketing step-up is already public. What is not public is whether Q3 overran again and how management frames 2027 investment. If this were fully priced, the stock would not have fallen on two consecutive EPS beats. The pattern is an inference from two quarters, not a document about Q3.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001746618/000119312526206442/rvlv-ex99_1.htm): marketing 15.8% against 14.3%. AAII (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/527118-what-you-need-to-know-about-revolve-group-incs-q3-earnings): 2 EPS estimate cuts and 0 raises in the last month. That is a different source pointing the same way on profit.

findings.finding: Sell-side targets were trimmed into the print, but ratings held. Raymond James cut its target from $28 to $25 (2026-10-16, Buy) and UBS from $29 to $27 (2026-10-27, Hold). Roth ($37, 10-21), Stifel ($33, 10-28) and BTIG ($35, 10-28) maintained or reiterated Buy. EPS revisions ran 2 down and 0 up over the month. A lowered bar slightly raises the odds that an in-line quarter is not sold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history. Before Q2 2026 targets were not cut, and the stock fell -4.06%.
findings.why_not_priced: These are public, so largely priced. The marginal point is that expectations drifted lower into the print rather than higher, which is the opposite of the Q1 and Q2 setups.
findings.independence: AAII revision count (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/527118-what-you-need-to-know-about-revolve-group-incs-q3-earnings), a different source. It overlaps with finding 4 on the revisions datum, which is used here only as evidence of a lowered bar.

findings.why_not_priced: The put OI may be stale hedges or written puts; the direction of those positions is not separable from OI alone. Shorts covering since July means less squeeze fuel than last year.

baseline_tension: The evidence leans mildly negative, in line with the stock's habit of selling prints (1 up of 7) and the put-heavy open interest. Against that, the falling short interest, analyst trims into the print and a 12% implied move (twice the median) say downside is already well hedged, so the lean stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold EPS beats in Q1 and Q2 2026): the reported-quarter positives were shrunk, revenue in line from +0.3 to +0.2 and GM conservatism from +0.8 to +0.5.
Lesson 2 (size one-offs as one-offs): the breach is a one-off the company calls immaterial and the $1.4M refund is a one-off inside the GM finding, so the breach went from -1.0 to -0.8.
Lesson 5 (an inference from a pattern is not a document): the opex-overrun guidance finding rests on two quarters' pattern, not a Q3 number, so it went from -1.2 to -1.0.

Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the revenue bar has two agreeing sources; the EPS sources disagree ($0.21 against $0.23), so the EPS-sensitive GM finding is capped small. No finding falls outside the window except the breach litigation, filed under outside_window.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest was looked up (6.84 days to cover, falling) and is not crowded, so the negatives keep their sign; put-heavy OI was kept as a small positive.
The net sum is unchanged at -0.5 because the cuts on positives and negatives offset. abs_move and p_up are unchanged.
